title: Mix the premix fuel
entry_state: Bike stopped, engine cool, in a ventilated place.
exit_state: Tank filled with fresh 30:1 premix, recorded.
completeness: Covers fuel choice, oil choice, the mixing ratio and filling.

required_parts.name: Premix oil
required_parts.purpose: Yamalube 2-R (Yamalube racing 2-cycle oil), or an equivalent type of oil if it is not available.

required_parts.name: Gasoline
required_parts.purpose: premium unleaded gasoline only.

critical_stop_conditions: Never run the engine on gasoline without oil.
Never mix two oil types in one batch.

steps.instruction: Write down the date, the fuel and oil you are using and the ratio.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Use fresh, name-brand premium unleaded gasoline only. Mix on the day of the race; never use premix that is more than a few hours old.
steps.title: Get fresh fuel

steps.instruction: Use Yamalube 2-R (Yamalube racing 2-cycle oil), or an equivalent type of oil if it is not available. Never mix two types of oil in the same batch.
steps.title: Choose the oil

steps.instruction: Mix the oil and gasoline at 30:1 (30 parts gasoline to 1 part oil) in a clean container. After an engine rebuild, use 15:1 for the break-in.
steps.title: Mix at 30:1

steps.instruction: Fill the tank with the mix. Tank capacity is 8.0 L (2.1 US gal).
steps.title: Fill the tank

steps.instruction: If you change oil types, drain the fuel tank and the carburetor float bowl of the old premix before filling with the new mix.
steps.title: Changing oil types

steps.instruction: If the engine knocks or pings, use a different brand of gasoline or a higher octane grade.
steps.title: If it knocks

steps.instruction: Write down the date, ratio, oil and fuel used.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Clean and oil the air filter
entry_state: Bike cool, on a stand.
exit_state: Clean, evenly oiled filter sealed in the airbox, seat refitted, recorded.
completeness: Covers seat removal, filter removal, washing, oiling, greasing and refitting.

required_tools.name: Air filter cleaner, kerosene or solvent

required_parts.name: Spare air filter element
required_parts.purpose: Fit if the old one is damaged.

critical_stop_conditions: Never run the engine without the element fitted.
Element not seated: do not start the engine.

steps.instruction: Clean and oil the air filter after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours); replace it as required. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Remove the seat.
steps.title: Remove the seat

steps.instruction: Remove the fitting bolt and washer.
steps.title: Remove the fitting bolt

steps.instruction: Take out the air filter element with the air filter guide.
steps.title: Take out the filter

steps.instruction: Clean the element in solvent and squeeze out the remaining solvent. Do not twist it; too much solvent left in makes starting poor.
steps.title: Clean the element

steps.instruction: Damaged: fit a new element.
steps.title: Check the element

steps.instruction: Apply Yamaha foam air filter oil or another quality foam filter oil and squeeze out the excess: wet but not dripping.
steps.title: Oil the element

steps.instruction: Fit the air filter guide to the element, lining up its projection with the hole in the element.
steps.title: Fit the guide

steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the matching surface on the air filter element.
steps.title: Grease the sealing face

steps.instruction: Fit the element so the projection on the guide lines up with the hole in the air filter case and the element seats properly.
steps.title: Fit the filter

steps.instruction: Fit the washer and fitting bolt and tighten it to 2 N·m (1.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the fitting bolt

steps.instruction: Refit the seat.
steps.title: Refit the seat

steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, filter condition and whether a new element went in.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check or replace the spark plug
entry_state: Engine cold, bike on a stand.
exit_state: Correct plug at the right gap and torque, recorded.
completeness: Covers removal, reading, cleaning, gapping and torque.

required_tools.name: Spark plug cleaner or wire brush

required_parts.name: Spark plug NGK BR9EVX
required_parts.purpose: Replacement plug.

critical_stop_conditions: Plug will not start by hand: stop and check the thread.

steps.instruction: Inspect and clean the spark plug after break-in, then every third race (about 7.5 hours); replace it as required. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Pull off the spark plug cap.
steps.title: Disconnect the plug cap

steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the spark plug.
steps.title: Remove the plug

steps.instruction: Worn or damaged electrode: replace it. Insulator should be medium to light tan; a distinctly different colour means check the engine condition. Long low-speed running makes it sooty even when all is well.
steps.title: Inspect the plug

steps.instruction: Measure the gap with a wire or thickness gauge: 0.6–0.7 mm (0.024–0.028 in). Standard plug: NGK BR9EVX. Out of range: regap it.
steps.title: Check the gap

steps.instruction: Clean the plug with a spark plug cleaner if needed.
steps.title: Clean the plug

steps.instruction: Clean the gasket and plug surface, screw it in finger-tight, then tighten it to 20 N·m (14 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the plug

steps.instruction: Push the plug cap on fully.
steps.title: Connect the plug cap

steps.instruction: Write down the plug reading, the gap and whether a new plug went in.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check and adjust the clutch lever free play
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Free play in range, locknuts tight, recorded.
completeness: Covers the free play check and adjustment at the lever and at the cable.
critical_stop_conditions: Clutch slips or will not free: do not ride.

steps.instruction: Inspect and adjust the clutch after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Measure the free play at the end of the clutch lever before the cable starts to work the clutch: 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in).
steps.title: Check the free play

branches.condition: Use the adjuster on the cable.
branches.label: Not enough adjustment

steps.instruction: Turn the adjuster at the lever until the free play is correct.
steps.title: Adjust at the lever

steps.instruction: Slide back the clutch cable cover.
steps.title: Slide back the cable cover

steps.instruction: Loosen the locknut on the cable adjuster.
steps.title: Loosen the cable locknut

steps.instruction: Turn the cable adjuster until the free play is correct.
steps.title: Adjust at the cable

steps.instruction: Tighten the locknut to 4 N·m (2.9 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the locknut

steps.instruction: Return the clutch cable cover to its place.
steps.title: Refit the cable cover

steps.instruction: Start the engine and check the clutch does not slip and frees fully.
steps.title: Test the clutch

steps.instruction: Write down the free play and anything you adjusted.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check, adjust and lubricate the drive chain
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Slack in range, wheel aligned, axle torqued, chain lubricated, recorded.
completeness: Covers measuring, adjusting with alignment, torque and lubrication.
prerequisites: Engine stopped; keep fingers away from the sprockets.
critical_stop_conditions: Chain too tight overloads the engine; too loose can skip and damage the swingarm.
Damaged chain or hooked sprocket teeth: replace before riding.

steps.instruction: Clean, lubricate and check the slack and alignment of the drive chain after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Put a stand under the engine so the rear wheel is off the ground.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Turn the rear wheel through several revolutions and check the slack several times to find the tightest point. Measure there.
steps.title: Find the tightest point

steps.instruction: Measure the slack above the seal guard mounting bolt. It must be 48.0–58.0 mm (1.89–2.28 in).
steps.title: Measure the slack

steps.instruction: Loosen the axle nut and both locknuts.
steps.title: Loosen the axle and locknuts

steps.instruction: To tighten the chain turn the adjusters counterclockwise; to loosen, turn them clockwise and push the wheel forward. Turn each side exactly the same, using the marks on both sides.
steps.title: Turn the adjusters

steps.instruction: Look from the rear: the chain must run in line with the sprocket.
steps.title: Check the alignment

steps.instruction: Tighten the axle nut to 125 N·m (90 lb·ft) while pushing down on the chain.
steps.title: Tighten the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the locknuts to 19 N·m (13 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the locknuts

steps.instruction: Measure the slack again at the tightest point.
steps.title: Recheck the slack

steps.instruction: Lubricate the chain with chain lube.
steps.title: Lubricate the chain

steps.instruction: Write down the slack before and after and the chain condition.
steps.title: Record the job

entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Slack in range, wheel aligned, axle torqued, chain lubricated, recorded.

steps.instruction: Clean, lubricate and check the slack and alignment of the drive chain after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Raise the rear wheel off the ground with a maintenance stand and make sure the bike cannot fall.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Shift the transmission into neutral.
steps.title: Select neutral

steps.instruction: Pull the chain up above the chain guide mounting bolt with a force of about 50 N (5.0 kgf, 37 lbf).
steps.title: Pull the chain up

steps.instruction: Measure between the chain guide and the bottom of the chain. It must be 48.0–58.0 mm (1.89–2.28 in) with the bike on the maintenance stand.
steps.title: Measure the slack

steps.instruction: Loosen the rear wheel axle nut.
steps.title: Loosen the axle nut

steps.instruction: Loosen both chain puller locknuts.
steps.title: Loosen the locknuts

steps.instruction: Turn both adjusting bolts by the same amount until the slack is right, so the wheel stays aligned.
steps.title: Set the slack

steps.instruction: Push the rear wheel forward so there is no gap between the swingarm end plates and the swingarm ends.
steps.title: Push the wheel forward
verification: No gap at the end plates.

steps.instruction: Tighten the rear wheel axle nut to 125 N·m (92 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the axle nut

steps.title: Tighten the locknuts

steps.instruction: Measure the slack again the same way.
steps.title: Recheck the slack

steps.instruction: Clean the chain and lubricate it with chain lube.
steps.title: Clean and lubricate the chain

steps.instruction: Write down the slack before and after and the chain condition.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check the brakes: lever, pedal, fluid, pads and hoses
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Brakes checked and set, recorded.
completeness: Covers lever and pedal position, fluid level, pads, hoses and a function test.

required_parts.name: Brake fluid DOT 4
required_parts.purpose: Only if topping up, same type as in the system.

critical_stop_conditions: Spongy lever or pedal: do not ride.
Brake fluid damages paint and plastic: wipe spills at once.

steps.instruction: Adjust the lever and pedal, check the fluid level and leaks after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours); replace the brake fluid every year. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: There must be no free play at the brake lever end. The standard lever position is 100 mm (3.94 in), adjustable within 86–105 mm (3.39–4.13 in).
steps.title: Check the lever position

steps.instruction: Remove the brake lever cover.
steps.title: Remove the lever cover

steps.instruction: Loosen the locknut, turn the adjusting bolt to the position you want and tighten the locknut to 5 N·m (3.6 lb·ft).
steps.title: Adjust the lever

steps.instruction: Refit the brake lever cover.
steps.title: Refit the lever cover

steps.instruction: Check the brake pedal position: 0.0 mm (0.00 in) from the top of the footrest to the top of the pedal. The adjusting bolt end must stick out of the adjusting nut but stay at least 2.0 mm (0.08 in) away from the pedal. To adjust, loosen the locknut, turn the adjuster and tighten the locknut.
steps.title: Check the pedal position

steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright with each reservoir top horizontal. Fluid at or below the lower level mark: add DOT 4 of the same type already in the system, keeping water out.
steps.title: Check the fluid levels

branches.condition: Replace the pads before riding and record it.
branches.label: Pads worn

steps.instruction: Apply the brake and look at each pad. Front pads: replace them as a set when the lining is down to the 1.0 mm (0.04 in) limit. Rear pads: replace them as a set when the lining is down to the 1.0 mm (0.04 in) limit.
steps.title: Check the pads

steps.instruction: Look for cracks, damage or wear on both brake hoses. Check the front hose clamp is tight. Hold the bike upright, apply each brake several times and look for leaks.
steps.title: Check the hoses

branches.condition: Air in the system: do not ride; have it bled and record it.
branches.label: Soft or spongy

steps.instruction: On a dry surface, use the front and rear brakes separately and check each works properly with no drag.
steps.title: Test the brakes

steps.instruction: Write down the fluid levels, pad condition and anything you adjusted.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Release built-up air from the fork
entry_state: Front wheel off the ground, fork fully extended.

steps.instruction: Remove the bleed screw on each fork leg and let the trapped pressure out.

title: Set the suspension back to the standard baseline
entry_state: Bike on a stand, suspension clean.

required_tools.name: Wrench for the fast compression adjuster

prerequisites: Suspension clean so the adjusters can be counted.
critical_stop_conditions: Never force an adjuster past its stop.
Left and right fork legs set differently: do not ride.

steps.instruction: Inspect and adjust the suspension after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours). Count and write down every current setting before changing anything. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Standard spring: red, 1 stripe paint mark. Its standard fitting length is 252.0 mm (9.92 in). Changing the preload on this bike needs the lower rear frame removed, which is not covered here.
steps.title: Check the shock spring

steps.instruction: Turn each fork rebound adjuster fully in, gently, then back it out 12 clicks (range 20 clicks out). Set both legs the same.
steps.title: Set fork rebound

steps.instruction: Turn each fork compression adjuster fully in, gently, then back it out 12 clicks (range 20 clicks out). Set both legs the same.
steps.title: Set fork compression

steps.instruction: Turn the shock rebound adjuster fully in, gently, then back it out to 10–13 clicks.
steps.title: Set shock rebound

steps.instruction: Turn the low compression adjuster fully in, gently, then back it out to 11–14 clicks.
steps.title: Set low-speed compression

steps.instruction: Turn the high compression adjuster fully in, gently, then back it out 1 3/8 ± 1/6 turns.
steps.title: Set high-speed compression

steps.instruction: With the tyres cold, set both to 100 kPa (15 psi).
steps.title: Set tyre pressures

steps.instruction: With a stand under the engine and the rear wheel off the floor, measure from the rear axle centre to the mark on the rear fender.
steps.title: Measure unloaded

steps.instruction: With the rider in full gear sitting on the seat, measure the same distance again.
steps.title: Measure with the rider

steps.instruction: Subtract the second measurement from the first. The standard figure is 90–100 mm (3.5–3.9 in).
steps.title: Work out the sag

steps.instruction: Write down every setting now on the bike, the sag and the tyre pressures.
steps.title: Record the job

steps.instruction: Check the rear sprocket bolts are not loose.
steps.title: Rear sprocket

steps.instruction: Check moving parts work smoothly; lubricate where needed.
steps.title: Lubrication

steps.instruction: Check the chassis and engine for loose bolts and nuts.
steps.title: Bolts and nuts

steps.instruction: Check the stator coil, CDI and ignition coil connectors are tight.
steps.title: Connectors

steps.instruction: Check the bike is set up for the track and weather and all maintenance is done.
steps.title: Settings

steps.instruction: Write down anything you adjusted or that needs attention.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Wash the bike and do the after-wash check
entry_state: Bike back from riding, engine stopped.
exit_state: Clean, dry, lubricated bike, recorded.
completeness: Covers protecting the openings, washing, drying, chain care and lubrication.
critical_stop_conditions: Water inside the airbox: dry it and service the filter before starting.
Brakes not biting after the wash: dry them before riding fast.

steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the date

steps.instruction: Let the engine and exhaust cool down.
steps.title: Let it cool

steps.instruction: Block the end of the exhaust pipe, for example with a plastic bag and a rubber band.
steps.title: Block the exhaust

steps.instruction: If the engine is very greasy, brush on some degreaser. Keep it off the chain, sprockets and wheel axles.
steps.title: Degrease if needed

steps.instruction: Rinse off dirt and degreaser with a garden hose using only enough pressure to do the job. Never use a high-pressure washer or steam cleaner.
steps.title: Rinse

steps.instruction: Wash all surfaces with warm water and mild detergent; use an old toothbrush for hard-to-reach places.
steps.title: Wash

steps.instruction: Rinse straight away with clean water and dry all surfaces with a soft towel.
steps.title: Rinse and dry

steps.instruction: Take the water off the chain with a paper towel and lubricate it so it does not rust.
steps.title: Dry and lube the chain

steps.instruction: Clean the seat with vinyl upholstery cleaner.
steps.title: Clean the seat

steps.instruction: Wax painted and chromed surfaces if you want; avoid cleaner-waxes with abrasives.
steps.title: Wax

steps.instruction: Take the cover off the exhaust pipe.
steps.title: Unblock the exhaust

steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle for several minutes.
steps.title: Run it

steps.instruction: Write down anything you found that needs attention.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Wash the bike and do the after-wash check
entry_state: Bike back from riding, engine stopped.
exit_state: Clean, dry, lubricated bike, recorded.
completeness: Covers protecting the openings, washing, drying, chain care and lubrication.
critical_stop_conditions: Water inside the airbox: dry it and service the filter before starting.
Brakes not biting after the wash: dry them before riding fast.

steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the date

steps.instruction: Make sure the bike has cooled down completely.
steps.title: Let it cool

steps.instruction: Block or cover the side cover air intake port, the hole at the bottom of the water pump housing, the hole at the bottom of the left crankcase cover, the silencer exhaust port and the end of each hose.
steps.title: Block the openings

steps.instruction: Make sure all caps, covers and electrical connectors, including the spark plug cap, are tightly fitted.
steps.title: Check caps and connectors

steps.instruction: Remove stubborn dirt such as burnt-on oil with degreaser and a brush, keeping it off seals, gaskets, sprockets, the chain and wheel axles. Rinse it off with water.
steps.title: Remove stubborn dirt

steps.instruction: Wash with warm water, mild detergent and a soft clean sponge, then rinse well. Do not aim a pressure washer or hose jet at wheel or swingarm bearings, fork or brake seals, electrical parts, the muffler, hoses or the air intake, and do not wash with the seat or covers removed.
steps.title: Wash

steps.instruction: Dry the bike with a chamois or absorbent cloth.
steps.title: Dry

steps.instruction: Dry the chain straight away and lubricate it so it does not rust.
steps.title: Dry and lube the chain

steps.instruction: Apply corrosion protection spray to metal surfaces, keeping oil and wax off the brakes, tyres, rubber and plastic.
steps.title: Protect metal

steps.instruction: Make sure there is no oil or wax on the brakes or tyres; clean the discs and pads with brake cleaner or acetone if needed. Test the brakes before riding fast.
steps.title: Check brakes and tyres

steps.instruction: Take the covers off all the openings you blocked.
steps.title: Unblock the openings

steps.instruction: Lubricate the cables, the brake and clutch lever pivots and the pedal pivots.
steps.title: Lubricate

steps.instruction: Write down anything you found that needs attention.
steps.title: Record the job
